title: Dual-Format Heading Extraction for HTML and Markdown Reports
description: This tour walks through the CLI changes made to support HTML-formatted library reports in the `hlx library show` command. Previously, the heading extraction regex in show.ts only matched Markdown headings (`# Title`). Since reports are switching to HTML format, a new HTML heading regex was added that runs first, with the original Markdown regex preserved as a fallback. No new runtime dependencies were introduced — the CLI remains zero-dependency by design. The local LibraryItemDetail type was also extended with an optional filePath field to align with the updated server API response.

steps.description: The `hlx library show` command is the single point of format-dependent logic in the CLI. The comment commands (comments-list.ts and comments-post.ts) are format-agnostic — they operate on anchor strings passed via --section and never parse report content. Diagnosis confirmed that only the heading regex in this file needed updating. All other CLI plumbing remains unchanged.
steps.title: Overview: Why show.ts is the Only File Changed

steps.description: The optional `filePath?: string | null` field is added to the local LibraryItemDetail type to align with the updated server API response (helix-global-server adds filePath to the library item endpoint). This field is marked optional for full backward compatibility — existing Markdown report consumers that don't receive filePath continue to work without any changes. The primary format-detection method is content inspection (HTML regex match), so filePath is supplementary context.
steps.title: Step L1: Add filePath to Local LibraryItemDetail Type

steps.description: The new HTML heading regex `/<h([1-6])(?:\s+[^>]*?id="([^"]*)"[^>]*)?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/i` is evaluated before the Markdown pattern for each line of report content. It captures three groups: (1) heading level 1–6, (2) the id attribute value if present, and (3) the raw inner text including any nested HTML tags. If this regex matches, the `id` attribute is used directly as the anchor slug when present — this is important because the updated agent prompts always emit `id` attributes on HTML headings, making slug generation deterministic and consistent with the client side.
steps.title: Step L2a: HTML Heading Regex — Tried First

steps.description: After a successful HTML heading match, a `continue` statement skips the rest of the loop body for that line. This ensures the Markdown regex at line 70 is never evaluated against a line that already matched as an HTML heading, preventing any double-processing or incorrect fallback. Lines that do not match the HTML pattern fall through naturally to the Markdown fallback below.
steps.title: Step L2b: `continue` Prevents Double-Processing

steps.description: The original Markdown heading regex `/^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/` is completely unchanged from the pre-implementation state. It only executes for lines that did not match the HTML pattern above. This guarantees full backward compatibility with existing Markdown reports — all legacy `hlx library show` behavior is preserved. The output format produced by both branches (level indicator, slug annotation, comment count) is identical, so callers and downstream display logic require no changes.
steps.title: Step L2c: Markdown Heading Regex — Preserved Unchanged as Fallback

steps.description: For HTML headings: the regex extracts the raw inner text (group 3), then `replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')` strips any nested HTML tags for clean display. The anchor slug comes from the `id` attribute (group 2) when present, falling back to `slugify(rawText)` only when no id attribute exists. The CLI's `slugify()` function (lines 15–22) differs slightly from the client's implementation (no 60-char truncation), but this only affects the edge-case fallback path. For all HTML headings generated by the updated agent prompts, the id attribute is always present and extracted directly, so slug consistency between CLI and client is maintained.
steps.title: Data Flow: HTML Regex → id Extraction → Slug Annotation

steps.description: The implementation is complete and minimal. Only show.ts was modified (3 atomic changes: filePath type field, HTML heading regex block, preserved Markdown fallback). TypeScript compilation passes with zero errors (`npx tsc --noEmit`). The CLI remains at zero runtime dependencies — a simple dual-regex approach was chosen over adding an HTML parsing library, which would have been over-engineering for single-element extraction. All existing comment commands (comments-list.ts, comments-post.ts) and the slugify utility are untouched. The major code paths for both HTML and Markdown reports are clean and regression-safe.
steps.title: Summary: Clean Code Paths, Zero New Dependencies
